title: ConsentRules
principles: Consent does not create authority beyond the grantor's authority.
Consent does not override constitutional, legal, safety, or policy constraints.
Consequential consent must be attributable and reconstructable.
Revocation takes effect according to the applicable contract and must prevent unauthorized future execution.
rules: Consent cannot be inferred solely from capability, presence, prior behavior or silence when explicit consent is required.
A revoked consent must not be used to authorize a new consequential action.
Historical actions remain reconstructable after consent revocation.
High-impact workflows must explicitly record whether human authorization and consent requirements were met.
